Prior and posterior state classification

Source: R/classify_states.R
classify_states.Rd

For each observation, returns the prior state probabilities (from the inflation components) and, for the estimation data, the posterior state probabilities (responsibilities), together with the maximum-a-posteriori state under each.

Usage

classify_states(
  object,
  rule = c("map", "threshold"),
  threshold = 0.5,
  newdata = NULL
)

Arguments

object

A fitted evzinb / evinb model.

rule

"map" (assign to the most probable state) or "threshold" (assign only when the top probability exceeds threshold, otherwise NA).

threshold

Threshold for rule = "threshold".

newdata

Optional data. Prior probabilities are always available; posterior probabilities need the response column and are NA otherwise.

Value

A tibble with prior_zero / prior_count / prior_evi, posterior_*, map_prior, map_posterior (factors with levels zero, count, evi) and y.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(genevzinb2)
model <- evzinb(y ~ x1 + x2 + x3, data = genevzinb2, n_bootstraps = 5)
#> evinf: using a data-driven candidate range for C_EV: [173, 263]. Pass `c.lim` / `control = evinf_control(c.lim = ...)` to override.
#> Warning: C_EV reached the boundary of the candidate range in 1 of 5 bootstrap replicates; consider widening c.lim.
classify_states(model)
#> # A tibble: 100 × 9
#>    prior_zero prior_count prior_evi posterior_zero posterior_count posterior_evi

#>  7      0.445       0.401    0.153           0.978         0.0223          0
